# Review 3: agent skills generated by `toolkit-nx:skills`

Reviewed: the generator source in `libs/toolkit-nx/src/generators/skills/`
(`skills.ts` and everything under `files/`), the installed copies in `.claude/`
and `.agents/`, and the generators the skills describe.

Since review 2, the generator has grown from one skill to three, plus a pointer
file:

- `development-workflow`: explore → scaffold → implement → verify → format →
  report, with `references/verification.md`
- `workspace`: how to explore the Nx workspace, and the feature layout
- `toolkit-nx`: the generator router and six references (mostly unchanged)
- `AGENTS.md`, copied to `.agents/AGENTS.md` and to `.claude/CLAUDE.md`

I checked the findings with a real run on `apps/test`: `feature orders`,
`page orderList`, `component order-card --translations=true`, and a dry run of
`pipe --feature=app`. Then I ran `nx run-many -t lint,test,build -p test`, which
is the check `development-workflow` asks for. I deleted the generated files
afterwards, and the working tree is clean.

## Verdict

**The process around the generators is now good. The generator output, and the
`toolkit-nx` references, are where it still breaks.** `development-workflow` and
`workspace` cover most of what reviews 1 and 2 said was missing: how to find the
project and feature, the layout, when to ask the user, affected lint/test/build,
and how to report back. The installed copies now match the source.

An agent that follows the skills exactly still finishes with a failing build and
failing tests that it did not cause, in this very workspace:

```
✔  nx run test:lint
✘ TS2307: Cannot find module './pages/orderList/order-list.page'      (R3)
✘ TS2307: Cannot find module '@storybook/angular'          ×2         (N1)
✘ TS7006: Parameter 'props' implicitly has an 'any' type.  ×2         (N1)
✘ NG0201: No provider found for `InjectionToken TRANSLOCO_TRANSPILER` (R2)
   order-list.page.spec.ts, order-card.component.spec.ts — 2 failed
NX  Running targets lint, test, build for project test failed
```

`development-workflow` now runs `build` as well, so the Storybook problem that
review 2 left unverified is now a confirmed failure.

## Remaining critical issues

### R3. Pages created with a non-kebab name produce a broken import, and the skill still says "kebab-case the project"

Reproduced with `--name=orderList`:

```ts
import { OrderListPage } from "./pages/orderList/order-list.page";   // folder is pages/order-list
export const routes: Route[] = [{ path: 'orderList', component: OrderListPage }];
```

`page.ts:22` and `page.ts:28` still use `options.name`, but `componentPath` now
kebab-cases the folder. So the generator itself writes an import that can't
resolve.

On the skill side, all six references still say **"Project name … convert to a
kebab-case"**. `--project` must match the Nx project name exactly: in a consumer
workspace a project might be called `myApp` or `@org/shop`, and
`readProjectConfiguration` throws for any other spelling.

**Fix:**

- Generator: use `names(options.name).fileName` for both the import path and the
  route `path` in `page.ts`.
- References: "`--project`: the exact name from
  `npx nx show projects --type app`. `--feature`, `--name`: kebab-case."

### R2. Translations: generated specs fail

`@jsverse/transloco` is now a dependency, so the compile error from review 2 is
gone. But `page.ts:10` still forces `translations: true`, and neither the page
nor the `--translations` component spec sets up Transloco:

```
NG0201: No provider found for `InjectionToken TRANSLOCO_TRANSPILER`.
Path: TranslocoService -> InjectionToken TRANSLOCO_TRANSPILER.
```

So every generated page, and every `--translations=true` component, fails `test`
right away. In a consumer workspace where Transloco is not installed at all, the
build fails too. `create-component.md:12-14` recommends `--translations=true`
without saying that it needs Transloco installed and configured.

**Fix:**

- Generator: when `translations` is true, have the spec template import
  `TranslocoTestingModule.forRoot({ langs: {}, translocoConfig: { availableLangs: [], defaultLang: 'en' } })`
  (or something similar). Expose `--translations` on the page schema instead of
  forcing it, or make it depend on `@jsverse/transloco` being in `package.json`.
- Skill: state the prerequisite, i.e. Transloco installed and provided in the
  app, and say that pages include it by default.

### N1. (New, confirmed) Every generated component, page and dialog breaks `build`

Every component, page and dialog gets a `.stories.ts` that imports
`@storybook/angular`. The workspace has `@nx/storybook` but **not**
`@storybook/angular`, and `apps/test/tsconfig.app.json` includes `src/**/*.ts`
and excludes only specs. So stories are type-checked as part of the app build:

```
TS2307: Cannot find module '@storybook/angular'
TS7006: Parameter 'props' implicitly has an 'any' type.   // render: props => …
```

`development-workflow` step 5 now runs `nx affected -t lint,test,build`, so an
agent hits this on the first component it creates. Then it either deletes the
stories, which undoes generator output, or it escalates. Nothing in the skills
mentions Storybook.

**Fix (pick one):**

- Generator: emit stories only when `@storybook/angular` is installed, or make
  it a `--stories` option.
- Workspace or app template: add `src/**/*.stories.ts` to `exclude` in
  `tsconfig.app.json`, and install Storybook where stories are wanted.
- Skill: at minimum, say that `.stories.ts` needs Storybook, and say what to do
  when it isn't set up.

### R4. Wiring a new feature into the app is still left to "the user"

`create-feature.md:3-5`: _"features are not wired automatically; the user should
add it manually."_ The reader is the agent. `development-workflow` now tells the
agent to _deliver the requested functionality_, and that conflicts with this
line: the agent will create a feature whose pages can't be reached, and then
report it as finished.

**Fix:** tell the agent to add the lazy route itself, and give the snippet. The
feature file exports `routes`:

```ts
// <sourceRoot>/app/app.routes.ts
{ path: 'orders', loadChildren: () => import('../orders/orders.routes').then(m => m.routes) }
```

## Important gaps

### N2. (New) `skills.ts` overwrites the user's `.claude/CLAUDE.md`

`skills.ts:25-32` runs `generateFiles` into `/.claude`, then
`tree.rename('.claude/AGENTS.md', '.claude/CLAUDE.md')`. In a consumer workspace
that already has a `.claude/CLAUDE.md` with its own instructions, running
`nx g @hexmode/toolkit-nx:skills` silently replaces it. Nx shows it as `UPDATE`,
which is easy to miss. `.agents/AGENTS.md` has the same problem.

Also, `.agents/AGENTS.md` is not a location that agents read automatically.
Codex and most other `AGENTS.md`-aware tools read `AGENTS.md` at the repo root
and in parent directories, not under `.agents/`. So for those tools, the "load
`development-workflow` first" instruction is never seen. Check this against the
agents you want to support.

**Fix:** if the file exists, append or update a delimited block (for example
between `<!-- toolkit-nx:start -->` and `<!-- toolkit-nx:end -->`) instead of
replacing it. Write the non-Claude copy to the root `AGENTS.md`, using the same
block approach. Add a spec for the "file already exists" case. The current
`skills.spec.ts` only checks that the files exist.

### N3. (New) The `workspace` skill invites `--feature=app`

`workspace/SKILL.md:170-171`: _"Folder `<sourceRoot>/app` is a feature called
`app`. This is a non-standard approach to Angular projects."_ Review 2 asked for
the opposite: exclude `app/` when picking a feature. A dry run confirms that
`pipe --feature=app` quietly generates into `src/app/pipes/x/`.

If `app` really is meant to be a feature (the shell: `app.routes.ts`,
`app.config.ts`, root component), say what belongs in it. For example: "only
app-wide shell artefacts; put domain code in its own feature". As written, the
sentence explains nothing to the agent, and "non-standard" reads like a warning
without saying what to do.

### N4. Libraries vs applications is still inconsistent

- The `toolkit-nx` description says "to an **application**".
- `workspace:125-128` says that features "apply both to Angular applications and
  Angular libraries".
- The generators work on any project with a `sourceRoot`.
- `development-workflow` step 3 forbids hand-writing for any new Angular
  artefact.

An agent asked to add a component to a library will not know whether to use the
generator. Pick one answer and state it in both `toolkit-nx` and `workspace`.

### R6. No fallback for artefacts without a generator

`development-workflow:29-31` and `toolkit-nx:18` say "do NOT hand-write" or "do
NOT use `ng generate`" without exceptions. The `workspace` skill implies guards
and interceptors are fine to write by hand, but it is not the skill the agent
reads at the moment of scaffolding. Add one line to `development-workflow` step
3: "If no generator covers the artefact (guard, resolver, interceptor, model,
…), write it by hand following the layout in `workspace`, and mention it in the
report."

### N5. (New) Error meanings and the dry-run check

Now that the generators throw, say what each message means at the point where
the agent runs them, in `toolkit-nx/SKILL.md` or the references:

- `Feature "x" does not exist.` → run the feature generator first.
- `Feature "x" already exists.` → reuse it.
- A correct page dry run shows five `CREATE` lines plus
  `UPDATE <feature>.routes.ts`.

Also add "use the page generator for pages, never `component --type=page`". It
creates the page but registers no route.

## Minor issues

- **`npx`:** `create-{directive,feature,page,pipe,service}.md` still use bare
  `nx g …`. `development-workflow` and `workspace` use `npx` everywhere, so the
  references are now the odd ones out.
- **Duplication:** the six references are still near-copies, differing only in
  the generator name. A command table in `toolkit-nx/SKILL.md` would remove a
  second file read for simple cases. Keep separate references only for
  `component` (`--type` / `--translations`) and `feature` (wiring).
- **Inconsistent command form:** `workspace` step 2 says
  `npx nx show project <project>`, but the section below says `… --web=false`.
  Use one form, preferably with `--web=false` (or `--json`), so that it never
  tries to open a browser.
- **Grammar in `toolkit-nx/SKILL.md`:**
  - description line 10: "Use instead of `nx g @nx/angular:*`, and
    `ng generate`, or hand-writing" → "instead of `nx g @nx/angular:*`,
    `ng generate`, or hand-writing the files".
  - line 18: "Do NOT use `nx g @nx/angular:*`, `ng generate`." → "Do NOT use
    `nx g @nx/angular:*` or `ng generate`."
  - all six references: "convert to a kebab-case" → "convert to kebab-case" (and
    see R3 for the project).
- **Leftover schemas:** `pipe-schema.json` and `directive-schema.json` still
  have `"$id": "Service"` and "Name of a new service". This was raised in both
  earlier reviews.
- **`verification.md` example projects** (`shared-ui`) don't exist in this
  workspace. That's fine as an illustration, but `npx nx run <project>:<target>`
  with the real project from step 1 would be less likely to be copied literally.
- **No drift guard** between `files/` and the installed `.claude/` and
  `.agents/` copies (from R1). The copies are in sync today only because someone
  remembered to regenerate them.
